To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 21 kDa component of the EBV capsid antigen is composed of two products of EBV genes BFRF3 (p21) and BLRF2 (p21), and that BFRF3 is associated with ZEBRA in EBV-positive B cells.
the 21-KDa component of the Epstein-Bar virus capsid antigen consists in part of a product of the BFRF3 gene.

the 21-KDa component of the EBV capsid antigen complex is a product of two EBV early genes, BFR3 and BLRF3; the BFRF3 gene product, but not BLRF2, fulfils the definition of ZAP21; and ZEBRA-associated p21 is not directly associated with ZEBRA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the 21-kilodaltlon components of the Epstein-Bar virus capsid antigen.
a new EBV capsid protein, the product of BFRF2, and the relationship of BFRF p21 to ZEBRA.
the identification of two EBV gene products which constitute the 21-kilodalt component of the EBV capsid antigen complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EBV BFRF3 gene product p21 is not a ZEBRA-associated p21.
the 21 kDa component of EBV capsid antigen is a product of the BFRF3 gene and that it may be coimmunopricipitated with ZEBRA in cells in which EB virus is lytically replicative.
BFRF3 encodes a 21-kDa protein that is a constituent of the viral capsids but does not directly interact with ZEBRA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the BFRF3 gene product, BFRF31 p21, is a component of the EBV capsid antigen complex, that the BLRF2 gene product, BLRF2 p21, is not, and that BFRF3, but not BLRF2, p21 can be coimmunopreipitated with ZEBRA.

the 21-KDa component of the EBV capsid antigen consists, at least in part, of the BFRF3-encoded product and is a ZEBRA-associated antigen only by virtue of its cross-reactivity with the ZEBRA-associated epitope on ZEBRA.
BFRF3 is a component of the EBV capsid antigen complex, is not a ZEBRA-associated antigen in cells infected with EBV, and may be a target for antiserum directed at the C terminus of ZEBRA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 21-KDa component of the EBV capsid antigen consists at least in part of BFRF2 and BFRF2 protein.

the 21 kDa of the viral capsids antigen is a complex of at least two proteins, BFRF2 and BFRF2, which are both expressed from late transcripts and present in virions but which have different properties and different relationships to the EBV Z protein.
EBV encodes at least two proteins that have a molecular mass of 21 kDa and that the BFRF3-encoded p21 is the only one of the two that can be considered ZAP21.
